last_transition_reason: The proof matches the lemma statement and establishes the desired bound by a standard gcd/residue-class decomposition. It shows the residues modulo n are distributed in blocks of size d and then counts the indices with residue at least j, yielding |S_{m,j}| <= n-j. No dependency violations or semantic drift are present.
latest_nl_proof:
Fix n>1, and let m be an integer with 0≤m≤n−1. Set d=gcd(m,n), and write m=da and n=db, so gcd(a,b)=1.

For each k∈{1,…,n}, let t_k be the least nonnegative residue of ka modulo b. Then ka=q b+t_k for some integer q, hence
km=dka=q(db)+d t_k=q n+d t_k.
So km is congruent to d t_k modulo n, and since 0≤t_k≤b−1, the number d t_k lies in {0,…,n−1}; therefore r_k=d t_k.

Now split k as k=qb+s with 0≤q≤d−1 and 1≤s≤b. For fixed q, the residues t_k are exactly the residues of sa modulo b as s runs through 1,…,b. Because gcd(a,b)=1, multiplication by a modulo b is a permutation of the residue classes modulo b, so the values t_k for one block q are a permutation of {0,1,…,b−1}. Hence each residue d t (0≤t≤b−1) occurs exactly d times among r_1,…,r_n.

Now fix j with 1≤j≤n−1, and put q=ceil(j/d). Then r_k≥j if and only if t_k≥q. There are exactly b−q integers t∈{0,…,b−1} with t≥q, and each occurs d times, so
|S_{m,j}|=d(b−q).
Since q=ceil(j/d), we have d q≥j, and therefore
|S_{m,j}|=d b−d q≤d b−j=n−j.
This proves that for every j∈{1,…,n−1}, the set S_{m,j} has cardinality at most n−j.
role_in_parent: Control how many indices contribute to each threshold level in the residue decomposition.
statement_nl: For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, let r_k be the least nonnegative residue of k*m modulo n for k = 1, ..., n. For each integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1, the set S_{m,j} = {k in {1,...,n} : r_k >= j} has cardinality at most n-j.

domain_restrictions: n must be a positive integer (to make 'modulo n' and least nonnegative residue well-defined over {0,...,n-1})
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n-1
r_k is constrained to be the least nonnegative residue of k*m modulo n, hence r_k lies in {0,...,n-1}
j is an integer satisfying 1 <= j <= n-1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n, for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, define for each k in {1,...,n} the least nonnegative residue r_k of k*m modulo n (so r_k is in {0,...,n-1}). Then for every integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1, the set S_{m,j} = {k in {1,...,n} : r_k >= j} has cardinality at most n-j.
